body: main.nuc (the App view: the router)  config.nuc  config/ (appConfig)  public/ (styles.css, favicon.svg)
shared/ models/ events/ components/ guards/ screens/
components/<c>/<c>_component.nuc        appcomponent: the facade, the only thing other components see

Calls allowed (N0301/N0302): screen → statemanager → appcomponent → usecase → repository/service.

rows.title: Platform `web` brief: Dragonfly web apps — Pieces
rows.summary: text, an element or a list.
body: - Attributes are the DOM's names: `className`, `onClick`, `onChange = (e) => ...`, `src`, `alt`; `children` is a
text, an element or a list. A list of views passes `key`. No JSX, no `class =`, no positional text.
- A view never omits `build() Element`; a `stateful` has fields, `initState()` and `setState(() => ...)`.
- Navigation by screen, never by address: `goTo(Screen, id = 7)`, `goBack()`. Inside a screen,
`Manager.method()` calls its provider; elsewhere `inject<CharactersComponent>()`.
- A statemanager has no generics (`statemanager M<S>` is N0218): the state model goes in `@stateModel(S)`.
- Events: `event Name` + fields; `Events.publish(Name(...))`; `useEvent(Name)` in `build`. Access: `guard` with
`canActivate()`, `@screen(acl = {...})`, `@acl(...)` on a use case. Not in this version: forms, translations,
the local database, plugins.
- Tests (`test/`, no word): `@mock([Repo])`, `when(Repo.method).thenReturn(Ok(x))`, `@test`, `@states("...",
expect = [...])`, `@widget` with `renderScreen(Screen())` and `~screen.findByText("...")`.

rows.summary: @before(loading) @state(CharactersState.full) loadPage(page: int) Result<CharacterError, Character[]> ~characters.getPage(page) // a view: its parameters are its props; build() Element; HTML functions with named attributes and `children` stateless CharacterTile(character: Character) build()…
body: @before(loading)
@state(CharactersState.full)
loadPage(page: int) Result<CharacterError, Character[]>
~characters.getPage(page)
// a view: its parameters are its props; build() Element; HTML functions with named attributes and `children`
stateless CharacterTile(character: Character)
build() Element
li(
className = "tile",
onClick = () => goTo(CharacterListScreen),
children = [span(className = "name", children = character.name), small(children = character.species)],
// a screen: @screen(route, providers, loggedIn, acl, notFound); <State>Builder has one callback per state
@screen(route = "/", providers = [CharactersManager])
stateless CharacterListScreen
build() Element
main(
children = [
CharactersStateBuilder(
loading = () => p(children = "Loading..."),
full = (list) => ul(children = list.map((c) => CharacterTile(key = c.id, character = c))),
error = (e) => p(className = "error", children = e.message),
button(onClick = () => CharactersManager.loadPage(2), children = "Next page"),

rows.title: Platform `web` brief: Dragonfly web apps — Pieces
rows.summary: // repository (data/): each method is an http call; :id goes to the path, other params to the query/body @repository(path = "character") repository CharacterRepository @get(path = ":id") getOne(id: int) Result<CharacterError, Character> @get(cache = true, ttl = 600000) getPage(page: int)…
body: ```nuclear
// repository (data/): each method is an http call; :id goes to the path, other params to the query/body
@repository(path = "character")
repository CharacterRepository
@get(path = ":id")
getOne(id: int) Result<CharacterError, Character>
@get(cache = true, ttl = 600000)
getPage(page: int) Result<CharacterError, Character[]>
@post(retry = 1)
save(character: Character) Result<CharacterError, Character>
// usecase (domain/usecases/): one method exec that returns Result; dependencies in the constructor line
usecase GetPageUseCase
(repository: CharacterRepository)
exec(page: int) Result<CharacterError, Character[]>
~repository.getPage(page)
// appcomponent (<c>_component.nuc): aliases to the use cases, never constructor parameters
appcomponent CharactersComponent
getPage() = GetPageUseCase.exec
// state model (state_models/): each field is a state of the screen; a boolean is a state without data
CharactersState
(full: Character[], error: CharacterError, loading: boolean)
// statemanager (managers/): @state(M.x) emits that state with the method's value; an Err emits `error`
@stateModel(CharactersState)
statemanager CharactersManager
(characters: CharactersComponent)
loadPage(1)
@state(CharactersState.loading)
loading()

rows.title: Platform `web` brief: Dragonfly web apps
rows.summary: A Dragonfly web app has only `.nuc` files and `public/`; the app is generated in `build/app` (never edit it).
body: A Dragonfly web app has only `.nuc` files and `public/`; the app is generated in `build/app` (never edit it).
You write the business logic; the framework writes the rest (components, DI, routing, JSON, states, http). The
platform's words are the mobile platform's (`repository`, `usecase`, `appcomponent`, `statemanager`, `@screen`); the
views are HTML functions. Full rules: `nuclear help web`; where each file goes: `nuclear help layout --platform web`.

rows.title: Platform `web` brief: Dragonfly web apps — Work cycle
rows.summary: 1. `dragonfly new <name> -p web` makes the project; put each file in its folder (the folder gives the kind).
body: 1. `dragonfly new <name> -p web` makes the project; put each file in its folder (the folder gives the kind).
2. Write following this sheet. A kind or decorator: `nuclear help <word> --platform web`; never guess one.
3. `dragonfly check` (or `nuclear check . --json`) until no errors, then `dragonfly test`.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 1. Project
rows.summary: `title` is the browser tab's title and `description` the page's description.
body: `title` is the browser tab's title and `description` the page's description. `public/` is served as it is: a
`public/styles.css` is the app's stylesheet and a `public/favicon.svg` its icon (the page links them when they exist).

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 1. Project
rows.summary: my_store/ ├── config.nuc dragonfly(platform = "web", dialect = "react"), app(...) ├── main.nuc the App view: the router with every screen ├── config/project_config.nuc appConfig: the connections and global services of the app ├── components/<name>/ appcomponent, config/, data/, domain/,…
body: my_store/
├── config.nuc                         dragonfly(platform = "web", dialect = "react"), app(...)
├── main.nuc                           the App view: the router with every screen
├── config/project_config.nuc          appConfig: the connections and global services of the app
├── components/<name>/                 appcomponent, config/, data/, domain/, presentation/
├── shared/                            models, events, guards, components, screens shared by the app
├── public/                            static files, copied as they are
└── test/*_test.nuc                    tests
`config.nuc` is the only manifest ([projects.md](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/spec/projects.md) §1): the platform and dialect, the app (name,
description, version) and the backends it talks to (`contracts(tasks_api = "../tasks_api")`: their models and
repositories are generated into `contracts/`, [projects.md](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/spec/projects.md) §1.2). `build/app` is the dialect's app,
never edited.
```nuclear
dragonfly(platform = "web", dialect = "react")
app(name = "my_store", title = "My Store", description = "A Dragonfly web app.", version = "1.0.0")

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 2. Kinds
rows.summary: Not in this version (STATUS.md, "Next" step 5): forms and `formmanager`, converters, translations, the local database (`@primary`, `saveLocal`), plugins and AI kinds.
body: | Area | Kinds and decorators | Rules |
| Views | `stateless`, `stateful` (params = props; `build() Element`; HTML functions `div`, `ul`, `button`...) | §3.1 |
| Configuration | `appConfig`, `config`; connection `Http(baseUrl, headers, timeout, interceptors)`; globals `SessionManager`, `Acl`, `NetworkManager` | §3.2 |
| Data | models (`@key`), `repository` with `@get`/`@post`/`@put`/`@patch`/`@delete` (`path`, `cache`, `ttl`, `retry`; `@path`, `@query`, `@body`) | §3.3 |
| Domain | `usecase` (`@requires`, `@acl`), `appcomponent`, `service`, `aggregate` | §3.4 |
| State | state models, `statemanager` (`@stateModel`, `@state`, `@before`, `@after`), `<Model>Builder` | §3.5 |
| Screens | `@screen(route, providers, loggedIn, acl, notFound)`, `goTo`, `goBack` | §3.6 |
| Events | `event`, `Events.publish`, `component` with `@on(Event)`, `useEvent` | §3.7 |
| Session and access | `SessionManager`, `Acl`, `guard` with `canActivate` | §3.8 |
| Tests | `tests` with `@test`, `@widget`, `@states`, `@mock` | §4 |
Not in this version (STATUS.md, "Next" step 5): forms and `formmanager`, converters, translations, the local
database (`@primary`, `saveLocal`), plugins and AI kinds. They come with the same words as the mobile platform.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3. Rules
rows.summary: 1. Golden rule: performance, speed and readability of the syntax.
body: 1. **Golden rule:** performance, speed and readability of the syntax.
2. **Only the business logic in Nuclear.** Components, props, registration in the injector, JSON, http calls,
state handling, routes and imports are written by the transpiler.
3. **Light clean architecture:** `data`, `domain` and `presentation` layers plus what is shared; the same
`N0301`/`N0302` rules as the mobile platform (§5).
4. **Closed components:** another component is used only through its `appcomponent`.
5. **The platform's runtime and the official ecosystem of the dialect:** http with cache and retries, state
managers, events, session, ACL, the router and the test helpers come from the dialect's runtime package; the UI
library, the bundler and the test runner are the dialect's.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.1 Views
rows.summary: A view's parameters are its props; `build()` returns an `Element`.
body: A view's parameters are its props; `build()` returns an `Element`. Elements are HTML functions with the
attributes as named arguments and `children` (a text, an element or a list), and other views called like
functions. A `stateful` keeps its fields while it is shown; `setState(() => ...)` changes them.
```nuclear
stateless CharacterTile(character: Character)
build() Element
li(className = "tile", onClick = () => goTo(CharacterDetailScreen, id = character.id), children = [
img(src = character.image, alt = character.name),
span(children = character.name),
stateful Counter(start: int = 0)
count: int = 0
initState() void
count = start
build() Element
button(onClick = () => setState(() => count = count + 1), children = "Clicked ${count}")

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.2 Configuration
rows.summary: `appConfig` (one per project) and `config` (per component) list `connections` and `globals`, as in the mobile platform.
body: `appConfig` (one per project) and `config` (per component) list `connections` and `globals`, as in the mobile
platform. `Http` is the http connection; `SessionManager(timeout)`, `Acl(inherits)` and `NetworkManager()` the
global services.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.3 Data
rows.summary: A `repository` is a class of http calls: the same decorators, parameters and return rules as the mobile platform (flutter.md §6.3): the path under the connection's `baseUrl`, `:name` from a parameter, the rest to the query (GET, DELETE) or the JSON body; a `Result` method answers `Err(E(message =…
body: A `repository` is a class of http calls: the same decorators, parameters and return rules as the mobile platform
([flutter.md](https://github.com/nuclearlang/dragonfly-mobile/blob/main/spec/flutter.md) §6.3): the path under the connection's `baseUrl`, `:name` from a parameter, the rest to
the query (GET, DELETE) or the JSON body; a `Result` method answers `Err(E(message = ...))`; `cache`/`ttl`/`retry`.
A model is its fields; it gets `fromJson`, `toJson` and `copyWith`; `@key` names a field in the JSON.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.4 Domain
rows.summary: `usecase` (one `exec` that returns `Result`; `@requires(internet, session)`, `@acl(roles, permissions, guards)`), `appcomponent` (aliases to the use cases), `service`, `aggregate`: identical to the mobile platform.
body: `usecase` (one `exec` that returns `Result`; `@requires(internet, session)`, `@acl(roles, permissions, guards)`),
`appcomponent` (aliases to the use cases), `service`, `aggregate`: identical to the mobile platform.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.5 State
rows.summary: A state model lists the states of a screen; a `statemanager` emits them (`@stateModel`, `@state`, `@before`, `@after`).
body: A state model lists the states of a screen; a `statemanager` emits them (`@stateModel`, `@state`, `@before`,
`@after`). The screen reads them with the model's builder: `CharactersStateBuilder(full = (list) => ..., error =
(e) => ..., loading = () => ..., orElse = () => ...)`, which re-renders on every state.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.6 Screens and navigation
rows.summary: `@screen(route = "/characters/:id", providers = [Manager], loggedIn = { forward: "/login" }, acl = { roles, permissions, forward: "/denied" }, notFound = true)` on a view: a route of the router; `:id` becomes the screen's parameter of that type, the other parameters come from the query.
body: `@screen(route = "/characters/:id", providers = [Manager], loggedIn = { forward: "/login" }, acl = { roles,
permissions, forward: "/denied" }, notFound = true)` on a view: a route of the router; `:id` becomes the screen's
parameter of that type, the other parameters come from the query. Every address is a new instance of its screen:
going from `/docs/a` to `/docs/b` builds the screen and its managers again. `providers` creates the managers for the screen
and its views, where `Manager.method()` uses them. `goTo(Screen, id = 7)` and `goBack()` navigate by screen, never
by address. The `App` view of `main.nuc` is the router.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.7 Events
rows.summary: `event Name` + fields; `Events.publish(Name(...))`; a global `component` method with `@on(Name)` runs with every one; a view calls `useEvent(Name)` in `build` to re-render on it.
body: `event Name` + fields; `Events.publish(Name(...))`; a global `component` method with `@on(Name)` runs with every
one; a view calls `useEvent(Name)` in `build` to re-render on it.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 3.8 Session and access
rows.summary: `SessionManager` keeps the session (token, user, roles, permissions, values) in the browser's storage and ends it after `timeout`; `Acl` gives role inheritance; a `guard` is a custom check for `@acl(guards = [...])`.
body: `SessionManager` keeps the session (token, user, roles, permissions, values) in the browser's storage and ends it
after `timeout`; `Acl` gives role inheritance; a `guard` is a custom check for `@acl(guards = [...])`.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — Generators
rows.summary: `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name>` writes the finished, compiling code of a resource (ADR-0103): its models (nested objects become models named `<Name><Key>`; a paged answer gives `<Name>Page`), the repository (an HTTP repository over the app's `Http` connection, a named one added when…
body: `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name>` writes the finished, compiling code of a resource (ADR-0103): its models

(nested objects become models named `<Name><Key>`; a paged answer gives `<Name>Page`), the repository (an HTTP repository over the app's `Http` connection, a named one added when the app has another), one use

case per action (`--actions list,get,search,create,update,delete`), their aliases in the facade, with `--screen <screen>` a screen that lists it with its state manager and state model, and a test with the repository mocked. The fields
come from an example answer (`--from-json <file|url>`), a spec (`--from-spec <spec.md>`: its example answer, else its
`Key | Type` table; a `GET https://...` line gives the API) or `--fields "id:int name:string"`. A file that exists is
never overwritten (the facade and the repository get only the members they lack, so an action added to a resource that exists is finished); a name another file declares stops it before it writes.
`dragonfly gen inspect` answers what the project has. The agent writes only what is not standard: a use case with
its own rules, a view's details.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — Generators
rows.summary: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name>` adds the alias of a use case the project declares to its component's facade; with `--calls <Repository>.<method>` it writes the use case too, when all it does is call that method of a repository.
body: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name>` adds the alias of a use case the project declares to its component's
facade; with `--calls <Repository>.<method>` it writes the use case too, when all it does is call that method of a
repository. What a screen shows of it (a state manager's method and its state) is written by hand.
```sh
dragonfly gen resource characters Character --from-json https://rickandmortyapi.com/api/character
dragonfly gen usecase characters CharacterEpisodes --calls CharacterRepository.episodes   # a method the repository declares

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 4. Tests
rows.summary: `tests` in `test/`: the app starts with its real config and every request answers what the test prepares (`DragonflyTest.respondWith`, `respond`); `@mock([Class])` makes a class a mock (`when(Class.method).thenReturn`, `verify`); `@test`, `@states` (the states a manager emits) and `@widget` (a…
body: `tests` in `test/`: the app starts with its real config and every request answers what the test prepares
(`DragonflyTest.respondWith`, `respond`); `@mock([Class])` makes a class a mock (`when(Class.method).thenReturn`,
`verify`); `@test`, `@states` (the states a manager emits) and `@widget` (a screen rendered in a memory router,
read with Testing Library's `screen`) as in the mobile platform; `beforeEach()`/`afterEach()` methods are the hooks.

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 5. Architecture
rows.summary: 5. Architecture
body: | Rule | Code |
| A `usecase` is only used from an `appcomponent` | `N0301` |
| A `service` is only used from a `usecase` or an `aggregate` | `N0301` |
| An `aggregate` is only used from a `usecase` | `N0301` |
| A `repository` is only used from a `usecase` or an `aggregate` | `N0301` |

| From another component (or from `shared/`, `config/` and `main.nuc`) only the `appcomponent`, the models, the events, the global components, the guards and the screens (`@screen`) are visible | `N0302` |
| Tests may use any declaration | — |

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly — 6. What the dialect decides
rows.summary: Only how it is written: the language, the UI library, the bundler, the test runner, the generated app and how to run it (react.md).
body: Only how it is written: the language, the UI library, the bundler, the test runner, the generated app and how to
run it ([react.md](react.md)).

rows.title: The `web` platform of Dragonfly
rows.summary: The web platform is the mobile platform in a browser (ADR-0097): the same words for the same things (`appConfig`, `repository` with `@get`, `usecase`, `appcomponent`, state models and `statemanager`, `@screen`, events, guards, tests), so an app's domain and state read the same on a phone and on…
body: > Inherits every rule of [nuclear-base.md](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/spec/nuclear-base.md) and the standard library ([library.md](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/spec/library.md)).
> This document defines the web platform (ADR-0093, ADR-0097): apps that run in the browser, written in Nuclear
> only. Today its only dialect is `react` ([react.md](react.md)); this document holds the platform's rules and
> kinds, `react.md` how React writes them. A project's Nuclear never changes between the dialects of the platform;
> only a use of a dialect's type definitions (a React hook, an npm package) ties code to that dialect.
The web platform is the **mobile platform in a browser** (ADR-0097): the same words for the same things
(`appConfig`, `repository` with `@get`, `usecase`, `appcomponent`, state models and `statemanager`, `@screen`,
events, guards, tests), so an app's domain and state read the same on a phone and on the web, and an agent that
knows one writes the other. What a browser has no use for (a native splash, workmanager, a secure keystore) is not
here; what it needs and a phone does not (HTML elements, a url bar) is.
